results.problem: Serre's cyclicity problem: unconditional positive density of primes p with E(F_p) cyclic
results.result: Claimed positive lower density c_E/(32 log 32) for every E/ℚ without full rational 2-torsion, CM and non-CM alike (known before under GRH, or for CM curves)
results.human_role: Human-led with AI writing: Bhargava's handwritten argument; GPT-6 added writing and details and helped with the Lean formalisation; builds on OpenAI's AI-generated analytic estimates
results.verification: Hexagon deposit, not refereed; partial Lean (deduction only); depends on unrefereed AI-era inputs

results.problem: Mézard–Parisi formula (2001) for the free energy of diluted spin-glass models, including random K-SAT
results.result: Claimed matching lower bound for diluted p-spin models with even p and random K-sat under symmetry and integrability assumptions, completing the formula (upper bound: Franz–Leone)
results.human_role: AI-found proof directed by the field's main expert: Panchenko asked for a new perturbation in his earlier argument; ChatGPT Astra found the proof; Panchenko rewrote it with ChatGPT Astra and Claude Fable
results.verification: Unrefereed preprint by a leading specialist; independent of OpenAI's own claimed proof (family 221)

results.problem: Erdős's question: is the number of C₄-free graphs on n vertices 2^{(1+o(1))ex(n,C₄)}?
results.result: Claimed affirmative answer (previous best upper bound 2^{1.0819…n^{3/2}}, Kleitman–Winston 1982)
results.human_role: Human-led: main ideas by the author; GPT-6 Pro helped complete the proofs; GPT-6.1 and Opus 5.5 revised the text
results.verification: Unrefereed single-author preprint

results.problem: Rate-optimality of AFEM with Dörfler marking for bulk parameters θ that are not small
results.result: Claimed rate-optimal convergence for every θ ∈ (0,1) (Poisson problem, conforming Lagrange elements)
results.human_role: AI-assisted: an interactive ChatGPT discussion with Storn produced the initial proof framework; the authors verified, corrected, generalised and rewrote it
results.verification: Unrefereed preprint by specialists of the field

results.problem: Maximal dimension of finite-volume (and of entirely ideal) right-angled hyperbolic polytopes
results.result: Claimed sharp bounds: 8 for finite volume (was ≤ 12), 4 for entirely ideal (was ≤ 6)
results.human_role: AI-assisted: models investigated proof ideas, helped strengthen the results and wrote and audited the Python and Lean code; the author wrote the paper
results.verification: Unrefereed preprint; Lean checks the logical deductions with geometric inputs as premises

results.problem: Optimal constant in the i.i.d. Berry–Esseen inequality (Esseen 1956 lower bound; sharpness conjecture attributed to Zolotarev, 1966–67)
results.result: Claimed: C_n ≤ C_E = (3+√10)/(6√(2π)) ≈ 0.40973 for every n ≥ 1, so the optimal constant equals Esseen's lower bound
results.human_role: AI-assisted: the two authors directed the reductions, certificate schemas and verification runs; AI systems helped with exploration, checking code, distributed verification and drafting; Hexagon text label 'primarily AI-generated', understanding 'some parts'
results.verification: Unrefereed Hexagon preprint with author-run exact certificates and a public Docker replay; no Lean proof of the full theorem; no independent check found

results.problem: Kervaire's conjecture (1960s; Kourovka 17.94) and the Kervaire–Laudenbach conjecture (Kourovka 18.87(a))
results.result: OpenAI's proofs accepted as solutions in the Kourovka Notebook after confirmation by N. V. Bogachev
results.human_role: Proofs from OpenAI's internal model run; human confirmation by N. V. Bogachev for the Notebook
results.verification: Expert-confirmed (Kourovka Notebook); Lean for the single-relator case; preprints not refereed

results.problem: Petty's equilateral-set conjecture (1971): every n-dimensional normed space contains n + 1 equidistant points
results.result: Claimed proof in dimension 5 (dimensions 3 and 4 were known)
results.human_role: Author wrote the prompt with a methodological hint; the agent generated the proof; the author organised, verified and rewrote it
results.verification: Preprint; not refereed

results.problem: Pure semisimplicity conjecture: every right pure semisimple ring has finite representation type
results.result: Claimed counterexample via a division ring extension with right dimension sequence (1, 2, 2, 2, …), through Simson's reduction
results.ai_system: GPT-6 Astra; GPT-6.1 Sol; Claude Opus 5.5
results.human_role: AI-assisted: GPT-6 Astra helped choose the criterion and construct the division rings; the author verified the proofs and completed the Lean formalisation with GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5
results.verification: Preprint; Lean 4 formalisation of the main theorem, public repository; not refereed

results.problem: Existence of the q-colourability threshold of G(n, d/n) (Achlioptas–Friedgut, 1999)
results.result: Claimed: for every q ≥ 3 a constant threshold d_q exists for G(n, d/n) (d_q/2 for G(n, ⌊cn⌋)), with an O(n(log n)^(−3/2)) hitting-time window
results.ai_system: Claude Opus 5.5; GPT-6 Astra; GPT-6 Luna; GPT-6.1 Sol
results.human_role: Authors supervised; the models did proof discovery, verification, Lean formalization and all writing; human understanding 'some parts'
results.verification: Unrefereed Hexagon preprint; Lean formalization claimed, not linked

results.problem: Spectral isometry conjecture (Mathieu–Schick 2002): unital surjective spectral isometries between unital C*-algebras are Jordan isomorphisms
results.result: Claimed full proof for arbitrary unital C*-algebras, plus the non-unital-map variant; Lean-checked per the authors (Palomar)
results.human_role: AI found the proof; the authors studied it, rewrote it as a human-readable paper and checked it
results.verification: Preprint; Lean proof registered on Palomar (PALOMAR-2026-10-28-000031); not refereed

results.problem: Optimality of the Euclidean algorithm among uniform processes (van den Dries–Moschovakis; Moschovakis's conjectured lower bounds for gcd and coprimeness)
results.result: O(log a/ log log a) remainder-call derivations of gcd, refuting the uniform-process forms of Moschovakis's conjecture and settling the closure-depth question negatively; the Main Conjecture for algorithms stays open
results.ai_system: GPT-6 Astra; Claude Opus 5.5; Codex; Claude Code
results.human_role: Contributor initiated and directed the work; GPT-6 Astra identified the result; the models wrote all text and Lean code
results.verification: Main bounds and refutations Lean-verified (Palomar comparator, 22 statements, two kernels); unrefereed Hexagon preprint

results.problem: How often do frontier models resolve randomly chosen open conjectures, and what do their resolutions contribute?
results.result: Candidate resolutions for 125 of 200 sampled conjectures (70 counterexamples, 55 proofs), 84% passing same-model review; many trivial, off-the-shelf or exploiting underspecified statements
results.ai_system: GPT-5.6 Sol; GPT-5.6 Sol Pro; GPT-6 Astra Pro
results.human_role: Researchers built the dataset and protocol and classified the outputs; no expert verification of the candidates
results.verification: Preprint; candidates checked only by LLM review

results.problem: Serre's 1960 conjecture: the Artin function of a finite group acting on a regular local ring with isolated fixed points is the character of an ℓ-adic representation
results.result: Proof in mixed characteristic, completing the conjecture (positive characteristic: Abe 2025; residue characteristic zero: classical)
results.human_role: Kisin directed the work; GPT Astra was used extensively to find the proofs and write the first draft; Kisin checked, refined and rewrote
results.verification: Unrefereed Hexagon preprint by a leading number theorist

results.problem: Laczkovich's Lipschitz mapping problem (1991): can every measurable set of positive measure in ℝ^d be mapped onto a cube by a Lipschitz map?
results.result: Claimed positive answer for every d (previously only d ≤ 2), plus Kolmogorov's contraction problem for Jordan measurable sets
results.human_role: AI-assisted: ChatGPT produced the key proposition and lemma; the author had the framework and lower bound, rewrote the proof and wrote the paper
results.verification: Preprint; not refereed

results.problem: Murty–Simon conjecture (Plesník 1975): diameter-2-critical graphs have at most ⌊n²/4⌋ edges, equality only for the balanced complete bipartite graph
results.result: Claimed proof for every n (previously known only for n beyond a tower-type bound, Füredi 1992)
results.human_role: AI-assisted: GPT-5.6 Sol found the n²/4 bound and the even-n equality case; the authors simplified it, proved the odd-n equality case and wrote the paper
results.verification: Preprint by two established combinatorialists; not refereed, no formal proof

results.problem: Classification of Finite Simple Groups (announced c. 1983, quasithin gap closed by Aschbacher–Smith 2004): formal machine-checked proof
results.result: Claimed complete, sorry-free Lean 4 formalization of the first-generation CFSG proof against TauCeti's statement, plus a repaired step in one published route to the Unbalanced Group Theorem
results.human_role: AI agents formalized the literature from a human-written blueprint; about 34 named mathematicians and engineers; experts Lyons and Solomon consulted
results.verification: Lean 4 kernel check claimed by the team (sorry-free, standard axioms); not yet independently rebuilt or audited

results.problem: Erdős–Lovász problem: the maximum size m(k) of an intersecting k-uniform family with covering number k; Frankl–Ota–Tokushige conjecture m(k) < (ck)^k
results.result: m(k) ≥ k^k·exp(−50√(k log k)) for log k ≥ 32, so m(k) = k^k·exp(−k^(1/2+o(1))) with Zakharov's bound; the Frankl–Ota–Tokushige conjecture is false for large k
results.human_role: AI found the construction; the authors verified the proofs, reworked the arguments and wrote the exposition
results.verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint

results.problem: Order of growth of the maximal Banach–Mazur distance R∞(n) from n-dimensional normed spaces to the cube ℓ∞ⁿ (Grünbaum's problem)
results.result: R∞(n) ≥ c·n^{2/3}(log 2n)^{−10}; with the Friedland–Naor–Youssef upper bound, R∞(n) = n^{2/3+o(1)}
results.human_role: Human-led: the author designed the strategy and stated the key proposition; GPT-6 generated its proof, which the author reworked
results.verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint

results.problem: Morgan–Mullen conjecture (1996): existence of a primitive completely normal element in every finite field extension; Hachenberger's lower bound
results.result: Claimed full confirmation of Morgan–Mullen (case n > q new, n ≤ q by Garefalakis–Kapetanakis) and of Hachenberger's bound for all (q, n)
results.human_role: AI-generated arguments, text, code and Lean under the author's direction; the author checked the proof by hand and the formal statements
results.verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint; Lean 4 formalization of the new case (with two cited results as axioms and compiler-trusted computation)

results.problem: Upper bound for the four-colour triangle Ramsey number R(3,3,3,3) = R₄(3)
results.result: R(3,3,3,3) ≤ 61 (previous upper bound 62 from 2004; lower bound 51)
results.ai_system: GPT-5.6 (Codex); Fable 5 (Claude Code); GPT-6 Pro; GPT-6 Astra (Codex)
results.human_role: Human-led computer-assisted proof; AI coding agents and models contributed reductions, the C case, experiments, formalization and editing
results.verification: Lean 4 formalization of the reductions plus SAT refutations by two independent solvers (the SAT part is outside Lean); unrefereed preprint with a public reproduction package

results.problem: Sogge's local smoothing conjecture (1991) in all dimensions; consequences: Bochner–Riesz, Stein's restriction conjecture (interior of range), Kakeya maximal and set conjectures in ℝⁿ
results.result: Claimed proof of local smoothing for the Euclidean wave equation in every dimension n ≥ 2 with ε loss, with Bochner–Riesz, restriction in the interior of the range, Nikodym/Kakeya maximal bounds and full Hausdorff dimension of Kakeya sets as corollaries
results.human_role: Credited to 'OpenAI'; released as 'model output directly', with no named human authors and no designated reviewers
results.verification: Unrefereed manuscript; OpenAI lists Lean comparator statements for the main estimate and the corollaries (not checked by us); no expert assessment yet

results.problem: Golomb–Welch conjecture (c. 1968–1970): no perfect r-error-correcting Lee code in ℤⁿ for n ≥ 3, r ≥ 2
results.result: Claimed full proof, in both the lattice and the arbitrary-centre forms
results.human_role: AI-assisted: authors used ChatGPT to explore proof strategies and check calculations; the authors say they wrote all results and proofs
results.verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprints (2610.33983, 2610.34291); no formalization

results.problem: Propeller conjecture (Khot–Naor 2008)
results.result: OpenAI's every-dimension proof (Lean comparator statement) simplified by an expert, with equality cases characterised and the 3D computer search removed
results.human_role: OpenAI model produced the original proof; Heilman (a prior contributor to the problem) rewrote and improved it, using GPT-6 for manuscript preparation
results.verification: Lean comparator statement in OpenAI's repository; independent human proof posted on arXiv (unrefereed)

results.problem: Tokareva's conjecture on sums of two bent functions (and her derivative conjecture)
results.result: Disproved for every even n ≥ 8 (derivative conjecture for even n ≥ 10) with an explicit quartic counterexample
results.human_role: Agents found the counterexamples and proofs during an olympiad; humans checked every statement and formalized two key equations in Lean
results.verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint; partial Lean 4 formalization (Eq. 4.2, 4.7)

results.problem: Lower tail of triangle counts in sparse G(n,p); conjecture of Yufei Zhao and open problem of Janson–Warnke
results.result: Variational problem solved for every η ∈ (0,1): minimizers are constant or balanced two-block graphons, with a first-order transition at η* = 0.009217…
results.ai_system: GPT-6 Astra; Claude Opus 5.5; GPT-6.1 Sol
results.human_role: AI-assisted: authors expected the answer from Zhao's work; GPT-6 Astra suggested key proof strategies, Claude helped with the computer-assisted proof, models wrote parts of the verification code and Lean
results.verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint with validated numerics and a Lean 4 formalization

results.problem: Constructing a solution of the two-dimensional KPZ equation at criticality
results.result: Construction of the Critical 2D KPZ Process as the unique limit of centred log partition functions of critical 2D directed polymers, a functional of the Critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow; proved non-Gaussian.
results.human_role: Human-led with substantial AI input: authors supplied structure, literature and judgement; ChatGPT developed key estimates and proofs, some of which failed audit
results.verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint (2610.31614, ~80 pages plus appendices); checked by its eleven authors

results.problem: Barry Simon's multidimensional L² conjecture (Problem 8, 'Schrödinger operators in the twenty-first century')
results.result: False in every dimension d ≥ 2: smooth, bounded, nonnegative, arbitrarily small potentials satisfying the (even weighted) L² condition for which −Δ + V has only pure point spectrum on (0, ∞).
results.human_role: AI-assisted: authors chose the problem and suspected falsity; ChatGPT developed the construction and the extension to the full spectrum; authors rewrote the argument
results.verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint (2610.31637); checked by its authors

results.problem: Asymptotics of the Archimedean local height pairing in degenerations without assuming the Hodge conjecture
results.result: Removes the Hodge-conjecture hypothesis (and minor hypotheses such as reduced simple normal crossing fibres) from the author's asymptotic formula h(t) − ⟨W,Z⟩ log|t| = O(1)
results.human_role: AI outlined the argument and found a related p-adic theorem of Scholl; the author worked out the remaining details and wrote the paper, at his advisor's suggestion to try AI
results.verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint

results.problem: Nagata's conjecture on plane curves (1959)
results.result: For r ≥ 10 very general points in P², every nonzero curve of degree d with multiplicities m_i satisfies Σ m_i < d√r (claimed by OpenAI; reorganized and re-proved by Tevelev).
results.human_role: Autonomous AI proof (OpenAI release, no human author); Tevelev re-derived, simplified and presented it, using ChatGPT Astra only for editing and figures
results.verification: Re-proved in reorganized form by a named independent specialist (Jenia Tevelev, arXiv 2610.30050, presented in a UMass Amherst talk); unrefereed

results.problem: Barnette's conjecture (Hamiltonicity of cubic 3-connected bipartite planar graphs)
results.result: Every cubic 3-connected bipartite planar graph has a Hamiltonian cycle; indeed G − e is Hamiltonian for every edge e (claimed by OpenAI; written out and partly re-proved by Li).
results.human_role: Autonomous AI proof (OpenAI release); Zhentao Li re-derived it by hand with combinatorial replacements, using LLMs to read the preprint and format the note
results.verification: Lean formalization by OpenAI (statement not independently reviewed by us); re-proved in digested form by a named independent graph theorist (arXiv 2610.30490); unrefereed

results.problem: Hochster's small Cohen–Macaulay module conjecture (1973), domain form in equal characteristic zero; Eisenbud–Schreyer–Weyman Ulrich question (2003)
results.result: A 3-dimensional complete Noetherian normal local domain over C with no nonzero finitely generated maximal Cohen–Macaulay module (OpenAI); Anghel extends the obstruction to all dimensions ≥ 3.
results.human_role: Counterexample autonomous (OpenAI release), building on human preprints by Anghel, Lopez and Chen; Anghel's survey re-proves and generalizes it, with proofs drafted with ChatGPT and Claude
results.verification: Complete proof given in a survey by a named specialist (Anghel, arXiv 2610.30027), not independent of AI drafting; Lean scope note from OpenAI; nothing refereed

results.problem: Double-cap conjecture / Witsenhausen's problem on spherical sets without orthogonal pairs
results.result: For n ≥ 3, sets in S^(n−1) with no orthogonal pair have measure at most that of two opposite caps of radius π/4, with equality only for double caps (claimed)
results.human_role: Human-led paper with an assistive AI role; the separate Lean proof was produced almost entirely with AI-assisted tools
results.verification: Unrefereed preprint; separate Lean 4 proof (different argument) with Comparator and two kernels, statements written by the authors, self-assessed

results.problem: Linear MDS conjecture (Segre 1955; maximum length of MDS codes / arcs), even characteristic
results.result: For q even and 2 ≤ k ≤ q, the maximum length of a k-dimensional linear MDS code over F_q is q + 1, or q + 2 when k ∈ {3, q − 1}
results.human_role: Human-led with AI tools: Kumar devised the argument and Claude helped formalize it in Lean; Chen and Huang used ChatGPT to explore proof strategies and check calculations
results.verification: Lean 4 proof (Mathlib, Comparator, three kernels) registered on Palomar; the Challenge statement adds two definitions (HasMinimumDistance, IsMDS) and was written by the AI agent; arXiv preprint unrefereed

results.problem: Borodin–Kostochka conjecture: χ ≤ max{ω, Δ − 1} for Δ ≥ 9
results.result: Claimed proof for all graphs with Δ ≥ 4583, lowering the explicit threshold from 5.3 × 10⁶; the range 9 ≤ Δ < 4583 remains open
results.human_role: Human-led with AI assistance on specific estimates, parameter optimisation and constructions (author's declaration)
results.verification: Unrefereed Zenodo preprint; rational-arithmetic checks with published code; not peer-reviewed or formalised

results.problem: Gale's conjecture (1953) on partitions of 3D sets into four parts of smaller diameter
results.result: A 101-point set in R³ whose every 4-partition has a part of diameter > 0.88928·diam, exceeding the sphere's 0.88807; first counterexample below dimension 9.
results.ai_system: GPT-6 Astra; GigaEvo (DeepSeek 4; Qwen 3 Max; Gemini 3; Claude Opus 4.6)
results.human_role: Human-led search; GPT-6 Astra co-developed the algorithms and heuristics (some proposed by the AI) that found the set
results.verification: Explicit finite object checkable in exact integer arithmetic (coordinates in Appendix A, verification scripts in the repository); unrefereed, no Lean

results.problem: Erdős–Szemerédi sunflower conjecture: k-sunflower-free families in 2^[n] have size at most c_k^n with c_k < 2
results.result: Claimed proof for every k ≥ 3, with the bound 2^((1 − 1/(16k³))n), via a new polynomial-method bound for vector sunflowers.
results.human_role: AI-assisted: the authors posed the generalization of Naslund–Sawin and rewrote the argument; ChatGPT 6 Astra Pro found the proof of the key Theorem 2
results.verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint; authors checked all results; the stated Lean 4.35 proof is not public yet (promised for Palomar)

results.problem: Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture (2-quasitraces / AW*-factors) and the monotone completeness conjecture for AW*-algebras
results.result: Counterexample to the quasitrace conjecture (from an unreleased OpenAI model, reproduced with a modified construction) and a finite AW*-factor that is not monotone complete
results.human_role: OpenAI model produced the original quasitrace counterexample; Arulseelan and Hanson re-derived it, devised the monotone completeness argument, and reworked GPT 6 Astra's preliminary write-up
results.verification: Quasitrace disproof reproduced by named independent experts in an unrefereed preprint; monotone completeness result unrefereed

results.problem: Arveson's hyperrigidity conjecture for operator systems in commutative C*-algebras (Davidson–Kennedy Question 8.4 setting)
results.result: Claimed commutative counterexamples, including a finite-dimensional one of affine dimension ≤ 129.
results.ai_system: GPT-6 Astra; Codex; GPT-6.1 Sol; Claude Opus 5.5
results.human_role: AI-assisted: human found the first example; GPT-6 Astra developed its initial proof and proposed the finite-dimensional example
results.verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint

results.problem: Irrationality exponent of the lemniscate period Ω = Γ(1/4)²/(2√(2π))
results.result: Claimed proof that the irrationality exponent of Ω equals 2, with a complete Lean 4 development.
results.human_role: Human-led with AI: Chudnovsky with ChatGPT for exposition and formalization, adapting OpenAI's AI-generated π method
results.verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint; complete Lean 4 proof in ancillary files, statement written by the author, built on OpenAI's unreviewed library

results.problem: Neumann–Zagier conjecture (1985) on tree lattices isometric to Z^n
results.result: Every positive definite tree lattice has an irreducible vertex; hence a tree presenting Z^n has a vertex of weight one
results.human_role: AI-assisted: Issa obtained the first proof of Theorem 1.1 with the two models; the authors digested, simplified and strengthened it and wrote the paper themselves
results.verification: Unrefereed preprint by named experts who checked and re-derived the AI argument

results.problem: n-queens constant bounds; sharpness of the Cohn–Elkies LP bound; Tuza's conjecture special cases; packing records
results.result: Claimed 120 records from an autonomous agent, including an ~84× narrower n-queens interval and certified non-sharpness of the Cohn–Elkies bound in dimensions 10 and 11
results.human_role: Agent-driven campaigns with human-set budgets and starting points from published methods; fixed verifier; humans wrote the report
results.verification: Unrefereed technical report with public certificates (dual vectors, witnesses); not independently checked

results.problem: Non-uniqueness of weak solutions of the unforced 2D Euler equations with vorticity in L^p, 2 < p < ∞ (beyond Yudovich's uniqueness class; the unforced form of Vishik's theorem)
results.result: Three independent claimed constructions of two distinct solutions with the same initial vorticity: vanishing-viscosity solutions for every p > 2 (Pappalettera–Sorella, fully AI-generated), renormalized weak solutions in L¹ ∩ L^q for every q < ∞ (Coiculescu, Lean-formalized), and finite-energy solutions in every finite L^p (Choi)
results.ai_system: GPT-6.1 Sol; Claude Opus 5.5; ChatGPT 5.6; ChatGPT 6.0; ChatGPT 6.1; GPT-6 Astra
results.human_role: Ranges from none (Pappalettera–Sorella: prompted only, no edits, no claim of authorship) to human strategy with AI-written details (Coiculescu: idea and strategy his, proofs, code and text largely by Claude; Choi: main ideas his, ChatGPT completed technical details)
results.verification: Unrefereed preprints (Hexagon, arXiv); Coiculescu reports a complete Lean 4 formalization with a Lean-verified interval-arithmetic checker, not independently rebuilt

results.problem: Erdős–Hajnal conjecture for H = P_t (induced paths), open beyond P5
results.result: Claimed proof that every path P_t (and the subdivided claws S_{1,2,t}) has the Erdős–Hajnal property; DeepMind's model and a Claude-assisted manuscript claim the P_t case independently.
results.ai_system: ChatGPT-6 Astra; Google DeepMind internal model; Claude Opus 5.5
results.human_role: Human-led (Nguyen): the author's framework, with Astra proving parts of key lemmas; DeepMind's and the Claude manuscripts are described as AI-generated
results.verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint; DeepMind's P6 proof verified by Joonkyung Lee with Lean (not yet public); the Claude manuscripts have Lean code but no expert review, and Zhou's Lean theorem is conditional

results.problem: Is every word-hyperbolic group sofic? (Hyperbolic groups were the leading candidates for sofic counterexamples after residual finiteness)
results.result: Claimed construction of a torsion-free two-dimensional word-hyperbolic group that is not sofic; independently, a claimed proof with Lean that OpenAI's non-residually-finite hyperbolic group is not sofic.
results.human_role: AI-assisted: AI-generated construction (Sandhu, 7 Oct) built on OpenAI's AI result; Thom reworked and checked the proof; GPT Astra helped draft
results.verification: Unrefereed preprint co-written by a sofic-groups expert (Thom); Douglas–Mghirbi's Lean formalization depends on OpenAI's unrefereed Lean development

results.problem: Brennan's conjecture (1978) on integrability of |g′|^p for conformal maps; Kraetzer's t²/4 conjecture for the universal integral-means spectrum
results.result: OpenAI's internal model proved Brennan's conjecture and disproved Kraetzer's conjecture at t = −1 (preprints dated 24 Sept, released 6 Oct). Four experts checked the work and gave a short independent proof that B_b(t) ≤ t²/4 on [−2, 2], strict except at 0 and ±2
results.human_role: AI-generated original proof; Binder, Ivrii, Prause and Smirnov validated it and wrote a shorter, stronger proof without AI help (some used AI agents to understand the AI proof)
results.verification: Lean formalization by OpenAI (per its scope note, not independently reviewed) plus an independent expert proof in an unrefereed arXiv preprint

results.problem: Gauss circle problem: the exponent θ in E(X) = O(X^θ)
results.result: θ ≤ 209/670 + ε ≈ 0.31194, improving Li–Yang's 0.314483 and going below Huxley's suggested 5/16 barrier for the Bombieri–Iwaniec method.
results.human_role: Human-led with AI tools: authors used ChatGPT and Codex to discuss proof strategies and to draft and check parts of the arguments; final proofs written and verified by the authors
results.verification: Unrefereed preprint; no formal proof

results.problem: Lonely Runner Conjecture (Wills 1967, Cusick 1973): every runner is at some time at distance ≥ 1/(n+1) from all others
results.result: ML(V) > (1+c)/(2n) for an absolute constant c > 0, the first constant-factor improvement over the union bound 1/(2n)
results.human_role: Human-led: authors developed the strategy; ChatGPT 6 Pro/Astra proposed the GCD-sum ingredient, pointed to Green–Walker, fixed gaps and turned informal proofs into rigorous ones
results.verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint

results.problem: Maximum number of Hamiltonian cycles (and paths) in an n-vertex tournament: Alon's question (1990) and Wormald's conjecture on the extremal tournament
results.result: C(n) = (cosh 1/cos 1 ± o(1))(n−1)!/2ⁿ, attained asymptotically by the cyclic regular tournament; asymptotic maximum number of Hamiltonian paths follows
results.human_role: Authors chose the problem and the strategy hint (permanent estimates); GPT-5.6 found the lower-bound proof and a second instance the upper bound; authors rewrote, simplified and exposited
results.verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint; human-written exposition of the AI proofs

results.problem: Existence of the Smith–Toda complex V(4); V(3) exists for p ≥ 7 (Toda)
results.result: V(4) exists for every prime p ≥ 11. OpenAI's internal model had shown it only for p = 1009, plus a V(n) at some prime for each n
results.human_role: OpenAI's model wrote the original papers; Angeltveit checked, simplified and extended them, using ChatGPT as an interactive assistant; he checked all arguments himself
results.verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint by a specialist; OpenAI papers expert-read, no errors found

results.problem: Lee–Loh–Sudakov conjecture on bipartitions with both directed cuts large; Scott's question on c(d)
results.result: Sharp bound ⌈(d−1)m/(2(2d−1)) + d²/(2(2d−1))⌉ for every d ≥ 2 and large m, ⌈m/6⌉ for d = 2 and all m, plus stability.
results.ai_system: Altifina framework; GPT-6 Astra; GPT-6.1 Sol; Claude Opus 5.5
results.human_role: AI-originated: the core proof (Theorem 1.2) was found by the multi-model framework; Tyomkyn revised and extended it with ChatGPT 6 Astra to the main theorems; humans wrote the paper

results.problem: Asymptotic value of Delsarte's linear programming bound for binary codes and spherical codes (Kalai's question)
results.result: Exact asymptotic rates of the binary and spherical Delsarte LPs for all distances, in closed form via elliptic integrals (matching upper and lower bounds).

results.problem: Hopf's conjecture: even-dimensional manifolds of positive sectional curvature have positive Euler characteristic (symmetric case)
results.result: Proved for manifolds and orbifolds admitting an effective isometric T³-action (previously T⁴), with the rational cohomology of fixed-point components classified.

results.problem: Gauss class number problem: list all imaginary quadratic fields of a given class number (effectively, unconditionally)

results.problem: Ghys's conjecture (1995): every holomorphic Anosov diffeomorphism of a compact complex manifold is conjugate to a holomorphic affine automorphism of a complex infra-nilmanifold
results.result: Proved in the codimension-one case: such maps are biholomorphically conjugate to hyperbolic automorphisms of a complex torus; this covers complex dimension 3.

results.problem: Hardy–Littlewood–Chowla conjecture, case Σ_{p≤x} µ(p+h) = o(π(x)) (Möbius on shifted primes; parity-problem model case)
results.result: Claimed: Σ_{p≤x} µ(p+2) = o(π(x)), and each sign of µ(p+2) has density 1/2 among primes with p+2 squarefree

results.result: Human-written exposition of the AI-found proof: for every rational r in [1, 2] there is a graph H with ex(n, H) = Θ(n^r).

results.problem: Amenability of Thompson's group F (Thompson 1973; Geoghegan's conjecture)
results.result: Claimed by OpenAI and re-proved in streamlined form by Kim and Lodha: F is nonamenable.

results.problem: Ulam's problem: is every Lie group countably representable (isomorphic to a group of permutations of a countable set)?
results.result: Yes: every Lie group, and hence every locally compact second countable group, embeds in Sym(N).

results.problem: Bloch constant conjecture: the Bloch constant equals the Ahlfors–Grunsky value 0.4718616…
results.result: Disproved: B < A_AG − 1.3 × 10⁻⁹.

results.problem: Quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions of arbitrary number fields
results.result: For every number field K, ζ_K has no zeros with Re s > 31/32; likewise finite-order Hecke L-functions over K.
results.human_role: AI-assisted: Cureton and Thorner directed the research and made the mathematical judgments; AxiomProver generated the proofs and the Lean formalization

results.problem: Erdős Matching Conjecture (1965); Łuczak–Mieczkowska–Šileikis tail-probability conjecture
results.result: Tail conjecture proved for all k; Erdős Matching Conjecture proved for fixed k ≥ 3, s sufficiently large, all n ≥ k(s+1).

results.verification: Unrefereed preprint; authors checked AI arguments

results.problem: Landau–Siegel zeros (exceptional real zeros of real Dirichlet L-functions)
results.result: Explicit version of OpenAI's claimed exclusion: (1 − β) log q ≥ 3.0 × 10⁻³ for every primitive real character of conductor q ≥ 3 (with Lu–Zaman–Zhao for small q).

results.problem: Skryabin's conjecture: every noetherian Hopf algebra has a bijective antipode
results.result: Proved, in the stronger form: finite uniform dimension on one side implies a bijective antipode.

results.result: Disproved for L_ω1,ω: an explicit sentence with exactly ℵ1 countable models and no perfect set of non-isomorphic models.

results.problem: Erdős Problem #1117 / Hayman Problem 2.16: can lim inf ν_f(r) = ∞ for the number of maximum-modulus points of a non-monomial entire function?
results.result: No: ν_f(r) > 2k only on a locally finite set of radii, with 2k sharp, so lim inf ν_f(r) ≤ 2k.

results.problem: Formal verification of Thurston's geometrization conjecture (posed 1982; proved by Perelman 2003 via Hamilton's Ricci flow)

results.problem: Smale's sixth problem: is the number of central configurations (relative equilibria) of the n-body problem finite for every choice of positive masses? Case n = 5 in the plane
results.result: Claimed: finitely many planar central configurations for every five positive masses, removing the codimension-two exceptional set of Albouy–Kaloshin.
results.human_role: AI-generated per the author's disclosure (AI found and proved the results, wrote the programs, the Lean formalization and the draft); the human role is not described

results.problem: Smallest Turing machines whose halting encodes Goldbach's conjecture, the Riemann Hypothesis and the consistency of ZF (Yedidia–Aaronson programme)
results.result: New record sizes: 21 states (Goldbach), 104 states (Riemann Hypothesis), 380 states (ZF), each proved in Lean 4 to be halting-equivalent to the previous record machine.

results.verification: Formal proof in Lean 4 (kernel-checked, comparator-audited); no paper yet

results.problem: Nirenberg's conjecture (1962): a negatively curved annulus bounded by convex curves in tangent planes contains no closed asymptotic curve
results.result: Counterexample: a smooth embedded annulus with negative curvature in its interior, convex boundary curves in tangent parallel planes, and two closed asymptotic curves.
results.human_role: Human-led with AI tools: AI models found a first counterexample for a discretized (hexagonal) version; the authors smoothed it and separately built the explicit construction in the paper
results.verification: Unrefereed preprint; explicit construction with computations verified in a Mathematica notebook

results.problem: Alon's problem: is a random permutation of length Cn² (posed with C = 1000) n-universal with high probability?
results.result: Yes with C = 32: failure probability at most exp(−cn/log n). The conjectured sharp constant 1/4 stays open.
results.human_role: Autonomous proof per the authors ('The proof was found by GPT-6 Pro'); the authors verified it and wrote it up
results.verification: Unrefereed preprint; proof checked by the authors

results.problem: Open Erdős problems (erdosproblems.com), open OEIS conjectures, Zanello's log-concavity conjecture, last-iterate rate of anchored GDA
results.result: Lean-verified resolutions of 9 of 353 attempted open Erdős (sub-)problems, 44 of 492 open OEIS conjectures, 2 of 4 open Hilbert-function problems, and an exact O(1/t) rate for anchored GDA.

results.verification: Unrefereed preprint; an independent OpenAI manuscript (family 041) claims the same theorem

results.problem: Erdős Problem #522 (1961): for a random polynomial with independent ±1 coefficients, does the proportion of zeros in the closed unit disk tend to 1/2 almost surely?
results.result: Yes, with a universal radial law ½(1 + coth x − 1/x) at scale 1/n and a variance formula showing non-universal fluctuations.

results.problem: Growth of the Hilbert number H(d), the maximal number of limit cycles of degree-d planar polynomial vector fields

results.verification: Lean 4 formalization (per the authors); unrefereed preprint

results.problem: Holomorphic Cancellation Problem (Derksen–Kutzschebauch 1998): if X × C is biholomorphic to C^(n+1), is X biholomorphic to C^n?
results.result: No, for some n in {4,…,8}, assuming the exotic affine space announced by Auroux, Bai and Pomerleano.

results.problem: Does the Partition Principle imply the Axiom of Choice? (Russell 1906)

results.problem: Exact overlaps conjecture for self-similar measures on ℝ (Simon 1996 for sets; Hochman 2014 programme), and the generalized entropy–Lyapunov dimension formula

results.problem: LeBrun–Salamon conjecture: every compact positive quaternion-Kähler manifold is a symmetric Wolf space

results.problem: Cyclicity conjecture: is the peripheral spectrum of every positive operator on a complex Banach lattice cyclic?

results.human_role: Human-led with AI tools: GPT-5.6 for editing, simplifying some arguments and the literature review; the author says all new contributions are his

results.verification: Unrefereed preprint; partial Lean auto-formalisation (main theorem modulo five literature inputs)

results.problem: Free group factor isomorphism problem (is L(F₂) ≅ L(F₃)?)
results.result: Claimed: yes; all interpolated free group factors L(F_r), 1 < r ≤ ∞, are isomorphic, with fundamental group ℝ₊.

results.verification: Unrefereed manuscripts; no formalization; no published expert assessment

results.problem: Borsuk's conjecture (1933): every bounded set in ℝᵈ can be partitioned into d + 1 sets of smaller diameter; smallest dimension in which it fails

results.ai_system: Codex; ChatGPT (GPT-6 Astra, reported); Claude (Fable 5.1, reported)
results.human_role: Human-led (Chow's group) with heavy AI code generation; the paper discloses automated assistance for proofs and prose
results.verification: Formalization of a known theorem, done twice: Chow group (kernel-checked, standard axioms only; proves the topological statement marked proof_wanted in Mathlib) and Frenzymath/PKU (full build, Comparator-checked against Mathlib-only target statements, re-checked with nanoda); neither paper refereed

results.problem: Zarankiewicz problem at density 1/2 and diagonal bipartite Ramsey numbers b(t,t)
results.result: b(t,t) = O(2^t); K_{t,t} guaranteed in balanced bipartite graphs of density 1/2 once N ≥ c·2^t.
results.human_role: AI-found proof after guided prompting; human rewrote and takes responsibility
results.verification: Unrefereed preprint

results.problem: Erdős problems #18(b), #859, #1062(ii) and Ben Green's open problems 24, 39, 40, as formalised on Conjectures.io
results.result: Lean 4 proofs accepted and paid by Conjectures.io; see key facts for each statement
results.human_role: AI-assisted: student solvers using ChatGPT/Codex for mathematics, certificates and Lean (disclosed for #108 and Green 24; not stated on every solution page)
results.verification: Lean kernel check against pinned bounty statements plus platform human review; no peer review; erdosproblems.com has not yet marked them solved

results.problem: Irrationality measure (exponent) of ζ(2) = π²/6
results.result: μ(ζ(2)) ≤ 5.0495243 (from 5.095412), fully formalized in Lean 4; later improved to < 5.0193784 (Niedbala Giraudin, Claude as technical assistant)
results.human_role: Human-led: Kleid ran the parameter search in his own CAS and directed the work; Claude wrote the Lean formalization
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean 4 (no sorry, standard axioms only); not peer-reviewed

results.problem: Planar Mumford–Shah conjecture (regularity of minimizing discontinuity sets)
results.result: Claimed classification of planar Mumford–Shah generalized global minimizers, which would imply the conjecture.
results.human_role: The human supplied his thesis, unpublished results and a research protocol; the model produced the proof text; checking by the author is ongoing
results.verification: Unverified claim, no expert review: preprint by the prompting author, who says his own check is ongoing; not formalised

results.problem: Odlyzko–Poonen conjecture on irreducibility of random 0/1 polynomials
results.result: Unconditional proof that random 0/1 polynomials are irreducible with probability tending to one, with the sharp asymptotic for the reducible probability.
results.human_role: AI-generated proofs and formalisation; the author directed the work, rewrote and checked it; an expert (Breuillard) checked the proof
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean 4, plus expert check; preprint, not peer-reviewed

results.problem: Courtade–Kumar (most informative Boolean function) conjecture: dictators maximise I(f(X); Y) under binary symmetric noise
results.result: Proved in full (all n, all noise levels, no balance assumption) by three independent teams on 21–22 Sep 2026; the Google–CUHK proof is computer-assisted and verified end-to-end in Lean.
results.ai_system: Gemini (Stellar Colosseum); ChatGPT; unnamed generative AI systems
results.human_role: Google–CUHK: humans supplied the reduction and the Bellman function, AI generated most new ideas and the region-by-region proof; Ky–Tran: human approach, ChatGPT developed the proofs; Mahdavifar–Beirami: AI generated the single-bit proof under human direction
results.verification: Google–CUHK proof formally verified end-to-end in Lean (per the authors); the others are unrefereed preprints

results.problem: Irrationality of ζ(5) = Σ 1/n⁵ (open since Apéry's 1978 proof for ζ(3); Euler-era question)
results.result: ζ(5) is irrational, with integer polynomials Q_n of degree 37n satisfying 0 < Q_n(ζ(5)) < exp(−139n²/5), and irrationality measure at most 260.
results.ai_system: Claude Opus 5; Claude Opus 5.5; Claude Code; unnamed generative AI tool (paper)
results.human_role: Paper by a single human author who discloses AI only for editing and consistency checks (disputed by Calegari). One Lean formalization was written by Claude agents directed by Dan Romik; the other, by Moritz Firsching, does not say how it was produced.
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean 4/Mathlib (two independent sorry-free formalizations; one checked by Comparator against DeepMind's Formal Conjectures statement, the other assumes the prime number theorem as an axiom); not yet peer-reviewed

results.problem: Chvátal's conjecture on intersecting subfamilies of downsets
results.result: Proof of Chvátal's conjecture via a sharp correlation inequality, followed by an AI-found short spectral proof and a Lean formalization.
results.human_role: AI-assisted, human-led original proof (ChatGPT tested inequalities and proved a guiding special case); the short spectral proof was found by GPT-6 Astra under human direction
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean (Codex-generated formalization of the Chang–Liu–Liu proof); preprints not yet refereed

results.problem: Goldbach-type problem for the Liouville function (Shusterman's question)
results.result: Every even N > 2 is a sum of two positive integers with Liouville value −1 (unconditional, all N).
results.human_role: Unknown; pseudonymous release with no first-party account of AI use
results.verification: Unverified claim, no expert review: pseudonymous Lean proof (build and axiom audit replayed by a third party, standard axioms only; the auditor says this is not mathematical peer review); AI role unverified

results.problem: Erdős problem #108: Erdős–Hajnal high-girth, high-chromatic subgraph problem
results.result: Negative answer: for every M there is a triangle-free graph with χ > M whose C4-free subgraphs are all 6-colourable (Kohlmeyer–Kruer, Lean-verified); improved to 3-colourable by Nguyen–Walczak.
results.human_role: AI-assisted: two Purdue authors developed the construction and the Lean proof with substantial ChatGPT/Codex help. In the follow-up, GPT-6 Astra found the proof of the 3-colourable lemma and the experts streamlined it.
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean 4 (Conjectures.io, against DeepMind's Formal Conjectures statement) plus an independent expert exposition (arXiv 2609.40192); the 3-colour improvement is an unrefereed preprint

results.problem: Sylvester's conjecture (1879): every prime p ≡ 4, 7, 8 (mod 9) is a sum of two rational cubes
results.result: Proved in full: the 4, 7 cases by Yin (arXiv 2605.25917, May 2026), the 8 case by Burungale–Tian (arXiv 2609.14893, Sept 2026), who show E_p: y² = x³ + p²/4 has analytic rank one; a shorter proof of the 8 case followed from Yin (arXiv 2610.08015, Oct 2026).
results.human_role: Human-led with AI tools. Burungale–Tian used ChatGPT and Claude for exploratory computations, editing and reorganization. In Yin's Oct 2026 short proof, the ideas are his and the detailed working-out was done by AI and then rewritten by him.
results.verification: Preprints on arXiv; not yet peer-reviewed; no formal verification

results.problem: Decidability of Medvedev's logic of finite problems
results.result: Medvedev's logic (and Skvortsov's logic) is undecidable.
results.human_role: Humans chose the problem and wrote structured prompts; ChatGPT found the core construction; the humans checked and rewrote it
results.verification: Unrefereed preprint; central argument verified in Lean by Claude Opus 5 (per the authors), not the whole paper; proofs checked and rewritten by the authors

results.problem: Dittert conjecture; Ibragimov–Iosifescu φ-mixing CLT conjecture; strong n-conjecture (n=4); Gamma–Theta eternal domination conjecture
results.result: One proof (Dittert, all n) and three disproofs, each with a Lean formalization or an explicit checkable counterexample.
results.human_role: Autonomous proof search in Epoch AI's harness; Tom Adamczewski directed packaging; Klostermeyer co-wrote the domination paper
results.verification: Formal proofs in Lean (mechanically checked). Statements and write-ups mostly not independently audited

results.problem: Inverse Galois problem for transitive groups of degree 24
results.result: Explicit polynomials over ℚ found for all ~25,000 transitive groups of degree 24 (as reported by Paderborn University).
results.ai_system: various participants' AI tools (not used by the winners for computation)
results.human_role: Crowdsourced competition; the winning team computed without AI
results.verification: Computer-checked submissions (Magma, PARI/GP)

results.problem: Upper bounds on the irrationality measure μ(π) (record 7.103205… since Zeilberger–Zudilin, 2019); spill-over to μ(ζ(3)) (record since Rhin–Viola, 2001) and μ(ζ(2))
results.result: μ(π) < 7.101862832357 via a two-exponent Zeilberger–Zudilin integral at A1 = A2 = 1857/2785; follow-ups give μ(ζ(3)) < 5.5138800 and μ(ζ(2)) < 5.0193784
results.human_role: AI-assisted: Bai credits GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6 Astra with help 'throughout' (parameter search, proof development and checking, computation, writing) and takes responsibility for the claims; Niedbala Giraudin credits Claude as technical assistant and checks every claim by independent computation
results.verification: Unrefereed preprints; computer-verified numerics (standalone verifiers for the follow-ups)

results.problem: Pierce–Birkhoff conjecture
results.result: Explicit continuous piecewise-quadratic function on R^30 that is not a finite lattice combination of polynomials; further counterexamples in dimensions 5, 6, 7, 22, 24 and 72.
results.ai_system: GPT-5.6; GPT-6; Claude Opus 5; Claude Fable 5.1
results.human_role: Humans gave high-level direction on which targets mattered and wrote the final exposition; a multi-model agent system found and reviewed the construction
results.verification: Lean formalisation of the counterexamples for n = 5, 6, 7, 30, 72 (repo 7pocheR/Pierce-Birkhoff; formal statement written by the authors' team, not independently audited); the n = 30 counterexample is presented as hand-checkable; unrefereed preprint

results.problem: Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness (Clay Millennium Prize problem), forced-breakdown case
results.result: Claimed proof, formalised in Lean, of finite-time blow-up for 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes with smooth external forcing.
results.human_role: Largely autonomous agent swarm; builds on human techniques of Córdoba and Martínez-Zoroa
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean (public) of the forced blow-up theorem; experts dispute whether this forced variant is the Clay problem that matters; Clay review pending; human peer review ongoing

results.problem: Köthe conjecture
results.result: Explicit counterexample disproving the Köthe conjecture, formally verified in Lean.
results.human_role: Autonomous discovery; humans checked and wrote up
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean 4 (repo tadamcz/koethe: Comparator-checked against the Formal Conjectures statement of Krempa's matrix form, standard axioms only, nanoda enabled); human write-up with ring theorists Böhmler and Marczinzik (arXiv 2609.07996) unrefereed

results.problem: Finite-time singularity for the unforced 3D incompressible Euler equations on R³ from smooth initial data
results.result: Numerically certified self-similar singular profile plus a (conditional) framework for its nonlinear stability; full rigorous blow-up proof not yet complete.
results.ai_system: physics-informed neural networks; OpenAI models and other LLMs
results.human_role: Human-led; AI (PINNs) discovered the candidate, LLMs simplified bounds and helped formalise derivations
results.verification: Interval-arithmetic certification of the profile; partial Lean formalisation; stability conditional

results.problem: Erdős problem #1122 (Erdős 1946): additive functions that decrease only on a density-zero set must be c·log n
results.result: Claimed proof that any real additive f with #{n ≤ X : f(n+1) < f(n)} = o(X) equals c·log n with c ≥ 0. Lean 4 formalization conditional on cited theorems. An expert in the area builds on it to settle Sárközy's 2001 local-extrema conjectures.
results.ai_system: GPT-6 Astra; GPT-5.6 Sol; Claude Opus 5
results.human_role: AI-led: by the disclosure, GPT-6 Astra proposed the proofs and wrote the Lean code; an anonymous human finished the manuscript. GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Opus 5 did editorial review.
results.verification: Preprint on Zenodo with a Lean 4 formalization that assumes cited results as hypotheses; used by a specialist (Mangerel) in follow-up work; not peer-reviewed; not marked solved on erdosproblems.com

results.problem: Collatz conjecture: lower bounds on the number of integers below X whose orbit reaches 1
results.result: A positive lower natural density of integers reach 1 within 10.46 ln n ordinary Collatz steps (linear count cX, with explicit but astronomically small c), improving earlier sublinear bounds X^0.84 and X^0.90.
results.ai_system: OpenAI GPT models via Codex; ProofAtlas.ai harness; Claude (manuscript review); AxiomProver (formalization of Kenny Lau's refinement)
results.human_role: AI-led: 'developed primarily by AI agents' with high-level guidance from Lech Mazur, who directed the work and is responsible for the claims
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean (ProofAtlas build: no sorry, standard axioms only); a refined version with explicit constants (Kenny Lau's paper, hexagonmath.org 2610.00249) was formalized by AxiomProver and checked with the Lean comparator against a Mathlib-only challenge reviewed by Lau ('author-verified'); not refereed; no published expert assessment

results.problem: Hopf's sign conjecture: closed even-dimensional manifolds with positive sectional curvature have positive Euler characteristic
results.result: Claimed smooth metric of strictly positive sectional curvature on S³×S³ (χ = 0), a counterexample in dimension 6; preceded by a claimed metric on S²×S³
results.human_role: Autonomous per the authors: the agent 'discovered' the metric and the proof; human authors posted and presumably edited the paper
results.verification: Unrefereed preprint; exact computer checks of finite identities in a public repository; not verified by geometers per Nienhaus–Wulle

results.problem: Formal verification of Fermat's Last Theorem (Wiles 1995)
results.result: First complete machine-checked proof of FLT from the axioms, in Lean 4.
results.human_role: Near-autonomous; occasional high-level guidance
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean

results.problem: Dying percolation conjecture θ(p_c)=0 for Bernoulli bond percolation on Z^d
results.result: Claimed Lean-verified proof that θ(p_c)=0 for all d ≥ 2, via a new additive gluing inequality that settles Kozma–Nitzan Conjecture 3.
results.human_role: Autonomous formalization: Claude wrote all the Lean code under Justin Leder's direction. The follow-up proofs of stronger conjectures were produced by GPT-5.6 Sol + Claude Fable 5.1 with 'minimal human intervention' from Ahmed Bou-Rabee
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean (mechanically checked); the statement's fidelity and the informal write-up are not yet refereed

results.problem: Erdős–Sós conjecture (Erdős problem #548)
results.result: Full proof: every n-vertex graph with more than (k−2)n/2 edges contains every tree on k vertices.
results.human_role: Autonomous discovery and Lean proof in Epoch's benchmark harness; humans checked, simplified and generalised it afterwards
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean 4; several independent human expositions; not yet peer-reviewed

results.problem: Erdős problems #1 (distinct subset sums), #74, #126 and #571 (rational exponents conjecture)
results.result: #1 disproved (N ≤ ε·2^n possible for arbitrarily large n); #571 proved (every rational α in [1,2) is a Turán exponent of a bipartite graph); #74 answered in the negative direction; #126 proved with |S(A)| ≫ n^(1/2).
results.human_role: Autonomous: the model worked in an agent harness without human steering; humans chose the problems, wrote the Lean statements and wrote informal expositions afterwards
results.verification: Formal proofs in Lean 4 checked against audited challenge statements; informal human digestion ongoing; not peer-reviewed

results.problem: Smale's mean value conjecture (1981), constant-1 form
results.result: Disproved: a polynomial with p(0) = 0, p'(0) = 1 and |p(c)/c| > 1 at every critical point exists (Lean). Follow-up: Smale's constant M > 1.1018.
results.human_role: Autonomous (benchmark run, no human steering); follow-up bound by Jatar & Ng with AI drafts rewritten by the authors
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean 4 (repo tadamcz/mean-value-problem: Comparator-checked against Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures statement, standard axioms only, nanoda enabled); the README's prose proof is machine-written and not human-checked; follow-up bound by specialists Jatar & Ng is an unrefereed preprint

results.problem: Bounded gaps between primes (toward the twin prime conjecture)
results.result: Claimed proof that infinitely many pairs of primes differ by at most 186.
results.human_role: Largely AI-generated per OpenAI
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean (announced); not yet independently peer-reviewed

results.problem: Matrix Spencer conjecture
results.result: O(√n) discrepancy for n symmetric n×n matrices of norm at most 1, achievable efficiently.
results.human_role: AI-assisted: humans chose the strategy and verified and polished; the model produced the key lemma's proof and most calculations
results.verification: Preprint; not peer-reviewed

results.problem: Large gaps between consecutive primes (Erdős–Rankin; Erdős problem #4)
results.result: Improved lower bound for infinitely many large prime gaps, saving a log log log n factor over FGKMT 2018.
results.human_role: AI-assisted: pseudonymous user DottedCalculator prompted the model; Thomas Bloom wrote the exposition
results.verification: Lean formalization of GPT-6 Astra's version reported; human expert review ongoing

results.problem: Hopf problem: does S⁶ admit an integrable complex structure?
results.result: Claimed explicit construction of integrable complex structures on S⁶ (answer: yes).
results.human_role: AI-assisted: human mathematician (Alpöge) directed and wrote up
results.verification: Lean formalisation reported; independent expert verification ongoing

results.problem: How large can the rank of an elliptic curve over Q be?
results.result: Explicit elliptic curve with rank at least 31, a new record.
results.human_role: AI-assisted search with human researchers (Alpöge, Howell)
results.verification: Independent points checkable by computer; listed by the rank record tables

results.result: Explicit C^∞ counterexamples: umbilics of index 1 + k/2 for every positive integer k, and a strictly convex smooth closed surface with exactly one umbilic (index 2); simplified independently by Ando and Umehara
results.human_role: AI-assisted: Alpöge and John-Paul Smith worked on the problem with Claude, which also checked it; Ando and Umehara used GPT-6.1 to search for candidate seed functions
results.verification: X-post announcement with explicit formulas; independent simplified construction in an unrefereed arXiv preprint by specialists (2610.34036); no formal proof

results.problem: Yau–Tian–Donaldson conjecture for constant scalar curvature Kähler metrics
results.result: Claimed explicit K-polystable polarized smooth projective fivefold without a cscK metric.
results.ai_system: Danus (Rethlas-based agent); Claude Fable 5 (Claude Code); GPT-5.6 Sol (Codex)
results.human_role: AI-generated main result with one key human redirection; the author checked and polished the text
results.verification: Preprint only; not formalised; not peer-reviewed

results.problem: Banach's isometric subspace conjecture
results.result: Real case completed (all odd n, with Gromov's even n); complex and quaternionic analogues also proved.
results.ai_system: ChatGPT 5.5 Pro; ChatGPT 5.6 Pro; GPT-5.6 Sol
results.human_role: AI-assisted: the humans made the reduction; the key approach came out of dialogue with ChatGPT Pro, and GPT-5.6 Sol drafted proofs that the authors checked and rewrote
results.verification: Preprints; not peer-reviewed

results.problem: Hadamard conjecture: a Hadamard matrix exists for every order divisible by 4
results.result: Explicit Hadamard matrices for all 12 previously unknown orders below 2000.
results.human_role: AI-assisted search directed by human researchers
results.verification: Computer-checkable constructions; independently verified and analysed by Egan, Kotsireas, London and Ó Catháin (arXiv 2610.27175)

results.problem: Proportion of nontrivial zeros of ζ(s) on the critical line (toward the Riemann hypothesis)
results.result: Unconditional proof that more than 67.2% of zeta zeros are simple and lie on the critical line.
results.ai_system: Claude (unreleased research model) in Claude Code
results.human_role: Near-autonomous: non-mathematician prompted; experts verified
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean (key results); expert review (Conrey, Goldston); independent re-proof

results.problem: Sendov's conjecture
results.result: Proof of Sendov's conjecture for all degrees, formally verified in Lean.
results.human_role: Human orchestrated (Mazur); Tao simplified and formalised with AI agents
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean; expert-checked by Tao

results.problem: Heil–Ramanathan–Topiwala (HRT) conjecture on linear independence of time-frequency shifts
results.result: Explicit counterexample: 12 time-frequency shifts of a Schwartz function are linearly dependent, disproving the HRT conjecture.
results.human_role: Human-led with AI assistance for strategy and parameter search; humans wrote and checked the proof
results.verification: Unrefereed preprint by specialists (Faulhuber, Petersen, van Velthoven, Voigtlaender) with certified numerics; v2 adds a purely analytic proof of a qualitative counterexample; Terence Tao posted a partial digestion; not formalised in Lean

results.problem: Period-index conjecture
results.result: Varieties of every dimension d ≥ 3 with a Brauer class of period 2 and index 2^d, contradicting the conjecture; a corrected conjecture is proposed.
results.human_role: Human-led: a wrong AI example inspired the construction; the human found and proved the correct one, with AI help on literature search and lattice calculations
results.verification: Preprint by an expert in the field; not peer-reviewed

results.problem: Schiffer's conjecture (Yau Problem 80) and the planar Pompeiu problem
results.result: Non-circular bounded planar domains carrying a nonconstant Neumann eigenfunction that is constant on the boundary, which disproves both Schiffer's conjecture and the Pompeiu conjecture in the plane (one explicit domain, and an infinite family).
results.ai_system: GPT-5.6; GPT-5.5; Claude Opus 4.8; Claude Fable 5; ChatGPT/Codex
results.human_role: Human-led. Colbrook–Stepaniants: AI only helped debug code. Cao-Labora–de Dios Pont: humans devised the bifurcation strategy; LLMs checked estimates numerically and drafted some lemma proofs, and GPT-5.6 wrote the Lean formalisation
results.verification: Computer-assisted interval certificate (Colbrook–Stepaniants); Lean 4 formalisation (Cao-Labora–de Dios Pont); not yet peer-reviewed

results.problem: Ten open problems incl. existence of explicit non-sofic groups, Connes rigidity, Erdős #146/#180/#183, sphere-packing bounds

Status varies by result

results.result: Proof that the numerical range W(A) is a 2-spectral set for every matrix A.
results.human_role: Autonomous: non-specialist prompted; experts verified
results.verification: Expert-checked (Crouzeix, Greenbaum, Townsend); preprint

results.problem: Optimal universal constant in the thin-shell (variance) theorem for isotropic log-concave distributions
results.result: Var(|X|²) ≤ 8n for every isotropic log-concave random vector in R^n, sharp for i.i.d. centered exponential coordinates; among uniform distributions on convex bodies the regular simplex is extremal.

results.result: Counterexample for n=5 (hence all n≥5); status now: true for n≤3, false for n≥5, open for n=4

results.human_role: Human-led; built by hand on an AI-assisted result
results.verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint (2607.22198); explicit counterexample, checkable by computation; the paper reports no AI use

results.problem: Rota's unimodality conjecture for the number of flats of a matroid by rank (and Mason's log-concavity conjecture)
results.result: Explicit matroids whose flat counts are not unimodal (Rota), not log-concave (Mason), and can have arbitrarily many peaks.
results.ai_system: ChatGPT 5.6 Pro; ChatGPT 5.5 Pro; Claude Opus 4.8
results.human_role: AI-assisted: humans directed the search and wrote the papers; ChatGPT found initial counterexamples/constructions that the authors generalized
results.verification: Explicit, checkable counterexamples in arXiv preprints; not yet peer-reviewed

results.problem: Dinitz–Garg–Goemans (Goemans) conjecture on the cost of unsplittable flows
results.result: Claimed counterexample: a small single-source, three-terminal instance with fractional flow cost 58 where every unsplittable flow with capacity violation ≤ 15 costs at least 60.
results.human_role: Rybin prompted GPT-5.6 Pro with a few short prompts; the model found the instance; Rybin published the chat
results.verification: Unverified claim (X post with chat log); arithmetic reportedly checked by others; no paper or peer review found

results.problem: Six open problems from the Erdős problems collection (numbers not identified)

results.human_role: Wang chose problems, wrote the prompts and acceptance criteria and audited outputs; GPT-5.6 Sol in Codex did the long searches and drafts
results.verification: Unverified claim (X thread); no database update or expert check found

results.result: Explicit non-injective polynomial map C³→C³ with constant Jacobian determinant, disproving the conjecture for all n≥3.
results.human_role: AI-assisted: human chose the problem and verified; Claude found the counterexample
results.verification: Explicit map, checkable by direct computation (constant Jacobian determinant and three points with the same image); digested and generalised by Terence Tao, Gallagher, Speyer and Shuhong Gao; no refereed paper by the discoverers

results.problem: Cycle double cover conjecture
results.result: Proof that every bridgeless graph admits a cycle double cover.
results.human_role: Autonomous proof per OpenAI; human experts wrote independent expositions
results.verification: Checked by independent graph theorists: Jim Geelen (notes, arXiv 2607.15399) and Sang-il Oum (exposition, arXiv 2607.16356); OpenAI's proof is a PDF, not refereed; a Lean formalisation is reported but not verified here

results.result: Deterministic lower bound Ω(d²/log(d+1)), matching Protasov's 1996 upper bound up to polylogarithmic factors.

results.result: A counterexample of order 4 not killed by 4, over a non-reduced base.
results.human_role: AI-assisted: Akhil Mathew directed the search and verified
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean (Mathlib)

results.problem: Erdős–Szemerédi sum-product conjecture (over R)
results.result: Finite sets of reals with both sumset and product set of size at most |A|^(2−c), disproving the conjecture over R; later reproduced autonomously by an AI agent.
results.human_role: Original disproof human-led, inspired by an AI result; follow-up shows autonomous AI rediscovery
results.verification: Unrefereed preprint by specialists (Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, Zhelezov, arXiv 2605.28781); the autonomous AI rediscovery is a separate unrefereed preprint (Huang, arXiv 2607.20525); no formal proof

results.problem: Erdős unit distance conjecture (planar point sets: at most N^(1+o(1)) unit distances)
results.result: Construction of planar N-point sets with at least N^(1+δ) unit distances for a fixed tiny δ>0, disproving Erdős's conjectured upper bound, via algebraic number theory; humans improved the exponent within weeks.
results.human_role: Autonomous discovery by the model; checked and refined by human mathematicians
results.verification: Expert-checked (Timothy Gowers and others); human follow-up papers

results.problem: McKean's conjecture on entropy along the heat flow; Gaussian completely monotone (GCM) conjecture
results.result: Explicit measure on R with positive 5th derivative of entropy under heat flow, refuting three related conjectures.
results.human_role: AI found the counterexample; humans verified and wrote the proof
results.verification: Unrefereed preprint (Gu & Sellke, arXiv 2605.11656) with a human-written proof; the multidimensional disproof by Zou, Fan, Gao and Wang (arXiv 2605.18081) is also an unrefereed preprint; no formal proof

results.problem: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.10; FrontierMath Tier 4
results.result: Resolution of a Kourovka Notebook group-theory problem with a human mathematician; state-of-the-art 48% on FrontierMath Tier 4.
results.human_role: Human-led with AI tools (Lackenby); benchmark autonomous
results.verification: Unrefereed preprint (arXiv 2605.06651); results checked by the collaborating mathematicians (e.g. Marc Lackenby), no independent check

results.problem: Erdős problem #1196 (Erdős–Sárközy–Szemerédi conjectures on primitive sets)
results.result: Proof of the conjectured bounds for primitive sets and divisibility chains, plus a new short proof of the Erdős primitive set conjecture.
results.human_role: AI-generated key idea from a non-expert's prompt; professional mathematicians verified and wrote the paper
results.verification: Unrefereed arXiv preprint (2605.00301) by eight authors including the specialists Jared Duker Lichtman and Terence Tao (both co-authors, so not independent checks); no formal proof

results.problem: Borsuk's conjecture: smallest dimension where it fails
results.result: Counterexample in dimension 63 (321-point three-distance set needing ≥ 65 parts), improving the 2013 record of 64.
results.human_role: AI-assisted: Max Grinsztajn worked with GPT-5.5 Pro; exact computer verification
results.verification: Explicit finite construction with an exact verification script and Sage-checkable certificates (no Lean); listed in Tao's optimization-constants repository; not peer-reviewed

results.problem: Erdős Problem #650: how many integers of a set A can always be matched to distinct multiples inside an interval of length 2·max(A)
results.result: f(m) = min(m, ⌈2√m⌉) for all m, settling the problem exactly
results.human_role: AI-assisted: ChatGPT proposed the strategy, Aristotle produced the Lean-verified argument; the authors simplified it and wrote the paper
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean by Aristotle (per the authors); human-written exposition in an unrefereed arXiv preprint; erdosproblems.com lists the problem as solved

results.problem: Lower bounds for classical two-colour Ramsey numbers R(3,k), R(4,k)
results.result: Explicit colourings improving nine long-studied Ramsey lower bounds.
results.human_role: Humans set up search and scoring; constructions found by AI
results.verification: Explicit constructions checkable by computer; arXiv preprint

results.problem: Formal verification of optimal sphere packing in dimensions 8 and 24 (Viazovska 2016; Cohn–Kumar–Miller–Radchenko–Viazovska 2017)
results.result: Complete Lean formalisations of both theorems, correcting minor errors in the published proofs.
results.human_role: AI-assisted: agent built on a human-started blueprint project
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean

results.problem: Decomposing the 3D torus digraph on m³ vertices into three Hamiltonian cycles
results.result: General explicit construction for all odd m, found by Claude and proved by Knuth.
results.human_role: AI-assisted: colleague Filip Stappers ran the Claude session; Knuth verified and proved
results.verification: Human proof by Knuth; formalised in Lean

results.problem: Open Erdős problems; conjecture in online optimisation; cosmic-string radiation calculations
results.result: Several Erdős problems solved autonomously, a decade-old online-optimisation conjecture refuted, and a new analytic technique for cosmic-string radiation.
results.human_role: Mixed: some autonomous; others in collaboration with 18 external researchers
results.verification: Batch of results in unrefereed preprints (arXiv 2602.10177 and companion papers), checked by the collaborating mathematicians, who are co-authors; one generalisation reported as peer-reviewed (not verified here). Status varies by result

results.problem: Erdős problem #728
results.result: Full solution of the intended version of #728, generated by GPT-5.2 Pro and machine-checked in Lean by Aristotle.
results.human_role: Near-autonomous: human relayed prompts between two AI systems
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean; endorsed by Terence Tao

results.problem: Erdős problems #124, #367, #707, #1026 and others
results.result: First AI-involved genuine new solutions of listed-open Erdős problems, including a full solution of #1026 and a Lean-verified autonomous proof for a variant of #124.
results.ai_system: Aristotle; AlphaEvolve; Gemini Deep Think; GPT-5
results.human_role: Mixed: #124 near-autonomous (formal statement given); #1026 human–AI collaboration
results.verification: Formal proofs in Lean for key steps; expert-checked (Tao, Bloom)

results.problem: Broad battery of optimisation-type open problems (e.g. inequalities, packings, finite-field Kakeya-type constructions)
results.result: Systematic evidence that LLM-driven evolutionary search matches or beats best-known constructions across dozens of problems.
results.human_role: Human-led with AI tools: mathematicians chose problems and scorers
results.verification: Explicit constructions checkable by computation (problem repository public); unrefereed arXiv preprint (2511.02864)

results.problem: Problems listed as 'open' on erdosproblems.com
results.result: No new mathematics: GPT-5 located existing published solutions to about 10 listed problems and partial results on 11 others.
results.human_role: Human researchers prompted literature search and publicised results
results.verification: Checked by Thomas Bloom (site maintainer)

results.problem: Finite-time singularity formation in fluid equations (Euler, Boussinesq, IPM)
results.result: Discovery of previously unknown families of unstable self-similar blow-up solutions, computed to near machine precision.
results.ai_system: physics-informed neural networks with Gauss–Newton optimisation
results.human_role: Human-led with AI tools: co-designed by mathematicians
results.verification: Numerical: high-precision computation of unstable self-similar profiles, not a computer-assisted proof; unrefereed arXiv preprint (2509.14185)

results.problem: Formalising the strong Prime Number Theorem (with error term) in Lean
results.result: Complete machine-checked formalisation produced largely by an AI agent in 3 weeks.
results.human_role: AI-assisted: agent wrote most Lean code from the human blueprint; humans supervised
results.verification: Formal proof in Lean (compiles against Mathlib)

results.problem: Convexity of the gradient-descent optimisation curve for L-smooth convex functions
results.result: A correct, novel proof of the bound η ≤ 1.5/L, improving v1's 1/L but weaker than the humans' tight 1.75/L result already posted.
results.human_role: Human posed the problem and verified the proof
results.verification: Informal proof checked by Sébastien Bubeck (OpenAI), who posed the question; not written up as a paper or refereed; the human authors' revised paper already had the tight 1.75/L bound

results.problem: 4×4 complex matrix multiplication (Strassen 1969: 49 multiplications); kissing number in 11 dimensions; ~50 open problems
results.result: 48 scalar multiplications for 4×4 complex matrices; kissing configuration of 593 spheres in 11D (previous 592); matched SOTA on ~75% and improved ~20% of 50+ problems.
results.human_role: Humans define the problem and an automated scorer; evolutionary LLM search autonomous
results.verification: Constructions verified computationally (independent GitHub checks); white paper, later arXiv

results.problem: Olympiad-level geometry proofs
results.result: 25 of 30 IMO geometry problems solved with human-readable proofs.
results.human_role: Autonomous
results.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature; proofs checked by an IMO coach (Evan Chen)

results.problem: Cap set problem: largest subsets of F_3^n with no three points on a line
results.result: Largest known cap set in dimension 8 (512 vs 496) and improved capacity lower bound.
results.human_role: Humans wrote program skeleton and evaluator; LLM-driven search autonomous
results.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature; constructions verified computationally

results.problem: Combinatorial invariance conjecture for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials; relations between knot invariants
results.result: ML-guided discovery of a conjectured, then proved, relation between the knot signature and hyperbolic invariants, and a new approach to combinatorial invariance for symmetric groups.
results.ai_system: supervised neural networks with gradient saliency
results.human_role: Human-led with AI tools: ML suggested patterns; mathematicians formulated and proved the theorems
results.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature; human proofs

results.problem: Several published conjectures on graph invariants
results.result: Explicit counterexamples found by an RL agent that treats building a graph as a game, rewarded by how badly the conjecture fails.
results.human_role: Human chose conjectures and reward functions; search autonomous; counterexamples trivially checkable
results.verification: Counterexamples checkable by direct computation; reimplemented by others (arXiv 2403.18429)
